rows.subtype: Shares a snack and comforts a friend [Actor]

rows.description: A child carries a classmate's bag when they are ill and keeps a secret they were trusted with; caring for people they know well is their strongest moral pull.

rows.description: A homesick student is brought tea and time by a flatmate without being asked, and feels safe; dependable small kindnesses tell people they belong.

rows.description: An adult helps family and friends generously, and also says no when exhausted, knowing that kindness that empties the giver cannot last.

rows.description: A child objects when a classmate from another community is left out of the game and says it is unfair; concern for justice reaches beyond friends.

rows.description: A teenager joins a tree-planting drive and worries about people far away who suffer from floods; wide concern grows with understanding of how the world is linked.

rows.subtype: Universal principle against loyalty to own circle [Actor]
rows.description: A young adult feels torn when principles of fairness for all conflict with loyalty to family or friends, and works through the tension instead of choosing carelessly.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.subtype: Turning wide concern into local action [Response]
rows.description: An adult volunteers, votes thoughtfully and treats neighbours from every background with respect, not just holding grand ideals; small consistent acts show the value at work.
